Fair that imagined what America would be like in the year 1960. This is of course meant to be ironic, but it winds up doubly so. “This World of Tomorrow,” which opened tonight at The Shed, is as old-fashioned as they come, like an overlong episode of an awkward early 1950s TV series.

A catatonic dullness and brace of stereotypical side characters further clog the pacing of This World of Tomorrow. Director Kenny Leon, who has recently had a string of Broadway hits, pulls out all the stops to keep this time-traveling misfire in the right galaxy. Even with brisk pacing and seamless scenic and projection design by Derek McLane, the play spins out of orbit, unable to connect its multiverse themes...
His latest endeavor, This World of Tomorrow, is a curious exercise in nostalgia by way of science fiction that trades on Hanks’ public persona without actually deepening it.
